items.prompt: Editorial documentary photograph of an empty early-1920s art-school workshop, captured with natural composition, true depth of field and soft morning light, then printed as a restrained two-tone image: deep ink black #161616 carries every shadow and form, warm paper white #F2EEE5 carries the light, with only a faint warm ochre #B8862B cast in the brightest highlights; a fine halftone dot texture appears in the mid-tone transitions and a subtle paper grain covers the whole frame, so it reads like a plate reproduced in an exhibition catalogue. Composition: a long room seen at a low three-quarter angle; in the left foreground a wooden hand loom strung with pale warp threads and a few spools of yarn on a bench; in the middle ground a metal workshop with a small lathe, a vise and a row of hammered brass bowls on a workbench; tall industrial steel-framed windows on the right throw long diagonal beams of light across the wooden floor; the far wall falls into calm shadow, leaving quiet dark margins around the edges that can be cropped. Strictly no people, no faces, no hands. Materials feel real: grain of the wood, sheen of brass, fibres of the threads. Quiet, still, precise, warm like an old photograph. Composed as a 1600x900 image for local use inside a rectangular window on the slide. NO text of any kind anywhere in the image — no letters, numbers, signs, watermarks, labels, posters or written symbols. Color values (HEX codes like #161616) and color names are rendering guidance only — do NOT display HEX codes, color names, or palette labels as visible text anywhere in the image.
items.alt_text: Empty Bauhaus-era workshop with loom and metal workbench in two-tone light
